p: A favorite neighborhood restaurant among locals with creative home cooking and friendly service. Vegan and gluten-free options. Not usually too noisy. Reservations recommended, especially on weekends.
Combination antique store and one of the best places to have a cosy high tea in the city. Pub fare also served. Minimum charge $12 per person.

Mitchell's has been serving the best ice cream and sorbets in SF since 1953. Choose from traditional fare or exotic flavors such as avocado, buko (baby coconut), guava, langka (jackfruit), macapuno (sweet coconut), mango, pineapple and…
Well prepared southern food. Fried chicken and fried okra are favorites.
Irish Pub. Excellent late weekend brunch no one knows about.
Organic produce and groceries, good bulk foods, and a deli with organic salads, Middle Eastern foods, and sandwiches to order. A neighborhood essential.
Expensive but wonderful "New American" cuisine with impressive artwork on the walls, and racy photography in the bathrooms. The macaroni and cheese is a must.
Considered one of the best local bakeries in the area. They supply some of the better SF restaurants as well as neighborhood demand for baked goods.
Gourmet Sardinian food, Italianate but often surprisingly spiced. Large list of unusual Sardinian and other Italian wines.
A fun, casual restaurant for hipsters. Do not expect fine dining or "authenticity" - just good spaghetti and big meatballs (the Caesar salad is delish, too). Beware the dangerous dive bar next door.
Neighborhood bar with strong, affordable, and creative cocktails. Owned by the same people as the Front Porch, across the street.
"opening hours differ by artist and may require appointment"

Unit Suite A, 3915 24th Street, San Francisco

Noe Valley Cuts and Shaves Barbershop

Buy a "slice" for under $3 or add toppings for a few cents more, and they'll make a fresh-to-your order triangular slice-shaped pizza that overlaps a dinner plate at three points. Free delivery. Cash or credit, no checks.
Decorated in dusty kitsch, the LAC also has large paintings for sale by local artists. They can offer up some of the best, strongest margaritas in town. Just one, that's all it takes.

One of the city's most popular parks, this is one of the main neighborhood hangouts, with people regularly partying or partaking in some recreational marijuana on its grassy slopes, as well as a sunny retreat for many San Franciscans…
Famous for their Indian masala pizza.
A quirky hipster bar with old arcade games and on some nights, live bands of varying talent.

A new cocktail bar serving outstanding Manhattans and other more unusual concoctions in a setting that feels like an old hunting lodge. A must if you like sipping bourbon and other aperitifs to old-timey music.
Carries hundreds of cheeses where you can taste before you buy.

California Chinese cuisine (e.g.: many vegs are fresh, white or brown rice, mu shu comes with grilled flour tortillas) with a nod towards Hunan and Mandarin styles. Tasty food in a bustling place. Accessible, vegetarian friendly, beer…
A neighborhood favorite with a full menu with many choices for various diets.
Excellent Thai food in a gay atmosphere, with some dishes that are not on the menu of most American Thai restaurants, such as Kao Soy, chicken with soft and crispy noodles in mustard sauce.
Good, not fanciful Chinese food, and quiet enough that you can talk to your dinner companions.
San Francisco's only cat café. Customers can play with cats while eating/drinking. Usually has 10-15 cats at a time, all of which are rescue cats.
A breeding ground for new performance, playwriting workshops, performances, a youth program, and classes. Some excellent one-person shows have been hatched out in the Marsh.

A nonprofit educational group and screening venue for independent film and video. This center often shows genuinely strange art films and videos, particularly during their frequent "open screenings" (you bring it, they'll show it).…
A theater with current popular movies, reserved seating and food and drink service.

Hipster-ed up diner, only open for lunch & breakfast. Long lines on the weekends, but surprisingly it moves quickly. Much better vegan breakfast option than Herbivore. Try the plantain cake and the mimosas.
Niman Ranch beef, or seitan veggie/vegan sandwich options. Great garlic fries!
Among the best coffee in the city. Organic beans roasted locally, each cup made fresh individually. A large seating area with free wi-fi.
